overview: This law gives a short-term extension to Section 702 and the rest of Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA), the authority that lets U.S. intelligence agencies collect the communications of foreigners outside the country, with help from American phone and internet companies. Those powers had been set to expire about two years after a 2024 law renewed them. This law moves the expiration date to April 30, 2026, giving Congress a little more time to debate a longer renewal and any changes. It also keeps in place the rules for winding down existing surveillance orders once the authority does expire. It became law on April 18, 2026.
for: Supporters say a brief extension avoids a lapse in an intelligence tool that agencies rely on to track foreign threats while Congress works out a longer-term bill.
against: Critics say extending the authority without changes continues a program that can sweep in Americans' communications without a warrant, and that short extensions put off needed privacy reforms.
